newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG LICK THEIR WOUNDS AND LOWER THEIR SIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG LICK THEIR WOUNDS AND LOWER THEIR SIGHTS.

text.p: Paris St Germain began a mini-revolution on Wednesday when managing director Jean-Francois Domergue announced he was taking a direct interest in the club's now disastrous sporting affairs.

At the same time, the players, smarting from a string of poor results, have lowered their sights from the championship title to a second place which would still qualify them for the coveted European Champions' League.

"The board of directors has entrusted me with a mission on the general running of PSG," Domergue told reporters at the Camp des Loges, the club's training headquarters where he plans to set up office.
"We have to get the club back on the rails, for the four months (remaining this season) and the coming seasons."

Domergue, who previously ran administrative matters and had no influence on team affairs, said: "We need more rigour and professionalism. The club has been affected in different sectors and we must reconsider our position.
"I'm going to be close to the sporting sector, while still retaining my present position... I won't be on the bench.
"What happened against Juve (a 6-1 home defeat in the first leg of the European Super Cup) was due to a sum of small details I'd prefer to keep to myself."

PSG's move points a finger of blame at sports director Jean-Michel Moutier, a former goalkeeper, who has played a major part in decisions on the transfer market -- decisions which have been severely criticised in the French sports media.

The weekly France Football listed a number of top rate players, including Real Madrid's Brazilian defender Roberto Carlos and the now Italy-based Christian Karembeu, Zinedine Zidane and Christophe Dugarry, who PSG appear to have let slip through their fingers in 1996.

It published a hypothetical team PSG might now be fielding which included promising new France international Ibrahim Ba, who looked set to join the club from Le Havre last year. Instead, he joined Bordeaux.

Only three of the current squad, goalkeeper Bernard Lama and central defenders Bruno N'Gotty and Alain Roche, were in the imaginary team and only Lama and N'Gotty played in the match against Juventus two weeks ago that sparked the crisis.
But Domergue said: "Jean-Michel Moutier is still the sports director and don't count on me to say a bad word about him.
"There might be a future redistribution of roles but first we must reassure our season ticket holders and supporters, who are legitimately disappointed. We have four months to start winning again."

"Shame on us because of you," read a damning banner posted by irrate fans outside the Camp des Loges on Tuesday, PSG's first day back after defeat in Sunday's top-of-the-table clash at Monaco which left them seven points adrift of the leaders.
Prior to the Juventus defeat, PSG dropped vital home points allowing Monaco to overtake them, but they believed their work during the winter recess would put them back on track for the title.
Instead, Sunday's defeat has given their next home game this weekend against lowly Cannes new meaning.
"We need a victory quickly. That would be something to lean on, a concrete way of making a new start. We must win a battle," PSG's Brazilian captain Rai said.
PSG have not won a significant battle since their 4-0 home victory over Galatasaray in the European Cup Winners' Cup second leg in October when they were 4-2 down from the away leg.
Since then, they have lost big games against Nantes, Juventus and Monaco, as well as falling to small fish like Nancy.

"The credibility of the players is in question and their confidence, as important as technique at this level, depends on a victory, whatever the manner," said Roche, who has been out through injury since December.
"Let's be realistic, the title is out of our hands... But the objective is to play the Champions' League next season, so we're going to hang on to this second place."
